catalog_meta.title: How do modular clinical enrichers (Temporal Anchors, CIEL & Public Standards Terminology KB, Tier-2 Retrieval, and Public Guideline Snippets) affect 32k chart reasoning across Gemma 4 (26B, 12B, E4B)?
catalog_meta.summary: Holding chart condensation constant at the 32k token sweet spot inside a 128k context window, we ablated five toggleable, prefix-cache-preserving clinical enrichers across three longitudinal patient records spanning all three condensation tiers: Margaret Chen (Tier 0 verbatim), Marcus Vance (Tier 1 run-length folded), and Maurice Auer (Tier 2 water-filled). Across 5 failure-mode clinical scenarios targeting active medications, brand-vs-generic statin duplication, therapeutic class overlap, missing-range critical labs, and adult vaccine series intervals (Q01, Q02, Q03, Q10, Q12; 15 cases x 15 modular arms = 225 total cells), we compared Verbatim Condensation alone against +Temporal Anchor & Trends, +CIEL & Public Standards Terminology KB (offline CIEL v2026-04-28 cross-walked with RxNorm, WHO ATC, CDC CVX/ACIP, and LOINC), +Core Enrichers (Temporal, Terminology KB, unseen-span Note RAG, and Overflow Recovery), and +Core Enrichers + Public Guideline Snippets ([K1]..[KM]) across Gemma 4 (26B, 12B, E4B) on an NVIDIA H200 (141 GB HBM3e) via Ollama on UW CIRG cobalt, graded blind by GPT-6.2 Sol (Codex CLI, reasoning high) and Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code CLI, reasoning high).
catalog_meta.takeaway: Combining deterministic chart-grounded enrichers in the Core Enrichers stack (Temporal Anchor & Trends, offline CIEL + RxNorm/ATC/CVX/LOINC Terminology KB, and Tier-2 Note RAG + Overflow Recovery) ranked #1 on both Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 26B while eliminating all confirmed harms (100% safety pass rate), whereas toggling external Public Guideline Snippets ([K1]..[KM]) exhibited a sharp model-scale crossover: unnecessary on 12B and 26B, transformative on 4B-effective E4B. Specifically, Gemma 4 12B + Core Enrichers @ 32k ranked #1 overall at 84.1/100 (83.4 safety-adjusted; 8.70 accuracy, 8.00 completeness, 8.70 relevance; 0 confirmed harms, 0 disputed, 15/15 fully supported citations; 6.45s median / 6.82s mean latency), gaining +7.6 Benchmark points (+10.0 safety-adjusted) over 12B Verbatim Baseline (76.5 Benchmark, 73.4 safety-adjusted, 1 confirmed harm). On Gemma 4 26B, Core Enrichers led at 79.8/100 (79.1 safety-adjusted; 8.13 accuracy, 7.87 completeness, 8.67 relevance; 0 confirmed harms; 4.26s median / 4.38s mean latency), +7.5 Benchmark points (+12.0 safety-adjusted) above 26B Verbatim Baseline (72.3 Benchmark, 67.1 safety-adjusted, 1 confirmed harm). Among single modules, the offline CIEL & Public Standards Terminology KB delivered the largest standalone lift at every scale (+3.6 on 26B to 75.9; +5.6 on 12B to 82.1; +15.1 on E4B from 59.3 to 74.4 with 0 confirmed harms), while Temporal Anchor & Trends alone slightly lowered scores on polypharmacy prompts without terminology disambiguation (68.5 on 26B, 68.3 on 12B) before synergizing inside Core Enrichers. Adding Public Guideline Snippets on top of Core Enrichers produced no net Benchmark gain on 26B (79.3 vs. 79.8, though lifting completeness to 8.13 with 0 harms and 0 disputed) or 12B (81.7 vs. 84.1), where parametric clinical knowledge already sufficed once brand/class mappings and vaccine series counts were resolved, but lifted Gemma 4 E4B by +8.7 Benchmark points over Core Enrichers (67.5) and +16.9 points (+23.8 safety-adjusted) over E4B Verbatim Baseline (59.3, 3 harms) to 76.2/100 (75.0 safety-adjusted, 0 harms; 4.69s median latency), surpassing unenriched 26B (72.3). Engine enrichment preparation averaged 43-73 ms across all profiles while preserving byte-identical system+chart KV prefixes, with 225/225 (100%) token-budget compliance, 1,494/1,504 (99.3%) inline citation resolution (100% across all three +Guideline arms), and blinded dual-judge Krippendorff's alpha of 0.600 accuracy, 0.600 completeness, 0.597 relevance, and 0.476 harm.
